- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., +0.2+), model often underreacts — increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 1–3% when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.3 → +0.2 → -0.4), model tends to lag — add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast smoothing.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often ignores sentiment decay — apply exponential decay to sentiment weights (e.g., 0.95 decay per day) to reduce noise.
